# Brilliantly Sane

> Contemplative psychotherapy with Lisa Wallace, LPC. Individual therapy by video across Colorado, based in Boulder. $175 for a 55 minute session, CO Access Medicaid accepted, free 20 minute consult.

Lisa Wallace is a Licensed Professional Counselor who graduated from Naropa University's Contemplative Psychotherapy program in 2017. She is WPATH trained, EMDR trained, Level I trained in Internal Family Systems, and a certified mindfulness instructor through Naropa and iBme. She works with individuals only, age 16 and up. She does not work with couples and does not prescribe medication.

## Core pages
- [About Lisa Wallace](https://losmanzanos.github.io/lisa/about/): background, training and credentials.
- [Therapeutic approach](https://losmanzanos.github.io/lisa/approach/): contemplative psychotherapy, IFS, EMDR, mindfulness, gender affirming care.
- [Who she works with](https://losmanzanos.github.io/lisa/work-with/): young adults 16 to 24, introspective clients, LGBTQIA+ clients, religious trauma.
- [Rates and payment](https://losmanzanos.github.io/lisa/rates/): $175 per 55 minute session, CO Access Medicaid, free consult.
- [Questions](https://losmanzanos.github.io/lisa/faq/): twelve common questions with plain answers.
- [Reach out](https://losmanzanos.github.io/lisa/contact/): free 20 minute consult, 970-368-9185, lisa@brilliantlysane.org.

## Journal
- [Meditation did not fix me](https://losmanzanos.github.io/lisa/journal/meditation-did-not-fix-me/): I came to practice because I'd run out of other ideas, not because it sounded restorative. What it actually did was more specific and less marketable.
- [The long middle of leaving a faith](https://losmanzanos.github.io/lisa/journal/the-long-middle/): Most writing about deconstruction covers the leaving or the landing. Almost none of it covers the years in between, which is where most people actually live.
- [Why I named the practice Brilliantly Sane](https://losmanzanos.github.io/lisa/journal/why-brilliantly-sane/): The phrase comes from Naropa, and from a stretch of my life when nobody would have described me that way. Here's what it actually means.
